description: Companies often fear that stronger privacy regulations will mean they’ll have less access to valuable consumer data. But an analysis of 16,000 U.S. customers using an engagement app found that after 2023 privacy laws took effect in California and Virginia, users in those two states divulged more data to the app overall and more diverse data than app-users elsewhere. Survey and search data indicate that clearer disclosures, consent mechanisms, and perceived safeguards increased trust among Californian and Virginian app-users—especially among those consumers most reluctant to share their data. For brands, robust privacy regimes can function like a low-cost incentive, expanding participation, improving data quality, and reframing privacy regulation from a compliance burden into a strategic asset.
title: How Stronger Privacy Laws Convinced Consumers to Share More Data
